title: SDK tutorial repro & quick fixes
body:
Daily scratch / repro notes (short, messy). Purpose: consolidate steps to reproduce two flaky tutorial issues, sketch quick doc fixes, and list next small tasks for the sprint. Will trim and move to a PR description once confident.

09:05 — context
- Running through 'quickstart-node' tutorial with a clean node:18 container and the newest @redwood/sdk (local linked build). Wanted to confirm examples still work after runtime changes to streaming and header auth.

09:17 — issue A: streaming chunk order inconsistent
- Observed: the streaming example in the tutorial sometimes emits the 'metadata' JSON chunk after the first text chunk. The tutorial prose assumes metadata comes first.
- Repro steps (minimal):
  1) docker run -it --rm node:18 bash
  2) npm i -g @redwood/sdk@next
  3) echo "const r = require('@redwood/sdk'); async function t(){const s=await r.streamGen({model: 'rw-small', prompt: 'say hi'}); for await (const c of s){console.log(JSON.stringify(c))}}; t()" > /tmp/x.js
  4) NODE_ENV=production node /tmp/x.js  # run 6 times, flaky
- Notes: Happens more on warm runtime after several requests. Hypothesis: router re-orders event envelope when upstream returns combined chunks.
- Quick doc fix: change tutorial wording to say "metadata may appear before or after the first text chunk; consumer should handle either order" and add simple aggregator snippet.

09:46 — issue B: sample-app auth example fails with local KMS var
- Observed: tutorial uses "REDWOOD_API_KEY" placeholder but my local env sets REDWOOD_KEY and the SDK silently falls back to unauthenticated client (no error). That leads to confusing 401s on server-side routes in the sample app.
- Repro steps (minimal):
  1) clone github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples
  2) cp .env.example .env && edit to set REDWOOD_KEY=bogus
  3) npm run dev -> client shows 401 on /api/generate with no helpful error in console
- Root cause guess: SDK env detection only looks for REDWOOD_API_KEY and does a falsey check; there is no warning when any auth is missing.
- Quick fixes:
  - SDK: add a runtime warning when neither REDWOOD_API_KEY nor REDWOOD_KEY (and other supported env keys) present. Put behind DEBUG flag. (small PR)
  - Tutorial: update env example to explicitly call out accepted env var names and show the local dev recommended: REDWOOD_API_KEY (preferred) and REDWOOD_KEY (legacy) with a note.

10:12 — small doc copy suggestions (to include in PR)
- Quickstart -> Step 2: replace "install global" with a npx example to avoid global install footguns: `npx @redwood/sdk@latest init` (one-liner)
- Streaming example: include tiny helper aggregate() that joins text chunks and merges metadata safely (pseudocode block).
- Add a short troubleshooting section called "If things don't stream" that lists 3 checks: API key present, correct Node >= 18, 2+ warm requests to rule out cold-start ordering.

10:37 — TODO list (priority order)
- [ ] Draft small SDK warning for missing env keys (Alex) — note: low-risk, add tests for console.warn + env combos.
- [ ] Edit quickstart tutorial copy for global vs npx and streaming caveat (me).
- [ ] Add aggregator snippet and paste into tutorial (me). Include a comment about handling metadata-after-text.
- [ ] Re-run sample-app dev workflow on mac + linux CI to confirm 401 messaging improved (Maya).
- [ ] Create GH PR with small changes, link to JIRA DEVX-721 (me).

11:05 — tentative PR description draft
- Title: doc(devx): make quickstart more robust and tolerant of streaming/auth edge cases
- Summary bullets:
  - Add environment-var warning in SDK when no supported auth is detected
  - Expand quickstart to include npx example, streaming caveat, and aggregator snippet
  - Update sample-app .env.example to show preferred and legacy env var names
  - Add a short troubleshooting section in tutorial

Outstanding questions to resolve before PR:
- Do we want SDK to be opinionated (throw) or friendly (warn) when auth missing? My vote: warn by default, allow throw in CI with REDWOOD_STRICT_AUTH=1.
- Where to keep aggregator snippet? Inline in tutorial or as a small file in sdk-samples/aggregators/aggregate-stream.js? I prefer samples folder so we can import.

Notes to self (implementation details):
- For env keys check on SDK bootstrap: check process.env.REDWOOD_API_KEY || process.env.REDWOOD_KEY || process.env.RW_TOKEN; if none, console.warn(`[redwood-sdk] No API key detected. Using unauthenticated client.`) - if REDWOOD_STRICT_AUTH set then throw.
- Tests: unit test around env detection, integration test that running sample-app with missing keys logs warning and client requests return 401 but with a clear message attachment in server logs.

End quick log. Will push initial draft edits to a branch `devx/quickstart-2026-03-13` after lunch and request reviews from Alex + Maya.

Links / references I pinged while testing:
- PR draft: github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-samples/pull/482 (local branch created)
- Jira: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DEVX-721
- Confluence (tutorial index): https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/DEVX/pages/12345/sdk-tutorials

Misc: record runtime logs to repro later: `node --trace-warnings /tmp/x.js > /tmp/trace-$(date +%s).log`

Quick mental checklist before PR: small CI green, unit tests for warning, tutorial wording approved by Maya, samples aggregated file added.
notes_summary: Two reproducible tutorial issues: streaming chunk order and env var/auth mismatch. Proposed short fixes: doc wording updates, small SDK env-warning, aggregator snippet, npx example. TODOs assigned to Alex, Maya, and me. Ready to branch and PR after tests.
